correctness.summary: The rising-sun level identity yields an exact one-sided Lp identity. A centered near-extremizer must nearly saturate both one-sided sharp inequalities; the exact identity converts this to near equality in Holder, and Lp uniform convexity gives quantitative one-sided near-eigenfunction rigidity. Pointwise domination transfers the estimate to the centered and dyadic-radii operators. Exact saturation forces a t^{-p} distribution tail and hence contradicts Lp integrability.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Madrid's 2026 source proves the exact centered norm and constructs extremizing sequences but does not state nonattainment or quantitative near-extremizer rigidity. Searches did not locate an equivalent centered result. Older nonattainment/eigenfunction work located in the review concerns the uncentered operator with a different sharp constant. A contemporaneous unindexed refinement remains possible, and the full 2010 uncentered paper was not independently rechecked.

value.summary: The result characterizes a necessary operator-level mechanism for every near-extremizer of the newly solved sharp centered inequality, settles nonattainment, extends the rigidity to the sparse centered-radii operator, and rules out strong compactness modulo natural affine symmetries.

limitations: The exponent 1/max{2,p} is not claimed optimal.
No spatial or multiscale classification of all extremizing sequences is obtained.
The compactness statement is not a full concentration-compactness theorem.
The dyadic-radii statement concerns the centered radii-restricted operator in the direct source, not the usual dyadic-grid maximal operator.
The full text of the 2010 uncentered eigenfunction paper was not independently rechecked.
A contemporaneous unindexed refinement may exist.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Cross-model review: not yet performed.
